## Objective

Get the project running on your machine, with your own keys, and prove it works
before spending any quota.

## Why this step exists

Most "it doesn't work" problems in a workshop are environment problems, not code
problems. We front-load them and give you a single command that proves the whole
setup is sound.

## Get the code

```bash
git clone https://github.com/dileepadev/deploying-agentic-ai-apps-workshop.git
cd deploying-agentic-ai-apps-workshop/app
```

The deployed application is its own uv project, so `app/` is where the rest of
this step happens.

## Install uv

[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) manages the Python version, the virtual
environment, and the packages — one tool instead of four.

<Tabs>
<TabItem label="macOS / Linux">


```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Windows">


```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Already have pipx or brew">


```bash
brew install uv        # or:  pipx install uv
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Then:

```bash
uv sync
```

That reads `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, installs the exact versions this
project was tested with, and creates `.venv` for you. **You never need to
activate it** — `uv run` handles that.

## Configure your secrets

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

Open `.env` (in `app/`, next to `pyproject.toml`) and fill in three values:

| Variable | Where to get it |
|---|---|
| `LLM_API_KEY` | [https://aistudio.google.com/apikey](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) → *Create API key* |
| `SUPABASE_URL` | Supabase → **Connect** (top of the dashboard) → *Project URL* |
| `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` | Supabase → **Settings → API Keys** → *Secret keys* → starts with `sb_secret_` |

One more is optional, and you can add it later without changing anything else:

| Variable | Where to get it | What it buys |
|---|---|---|
| `TAVILY_API_KEY` | [https://app.tavily.com](https://app.tavily.com) → free, no card | Web search, so the agent can answer questions about *this week* rather than only what Wikipedia has written up |

Leave it blank and everything in this workshop still works — the agent
researches with Wikipedia alone, and says so when asked about something
recent.

<Aside type="tip" title="Prefer a different model provider?">


Gemini is the default because it's the shortest path to a working key, but
Cerebras, OpenRouter and Groq are all free without a card, and switching is
three environment variables — no code change.

Follow the workshop on Gemini first — every screenshot and error message
below assumes it — then see [Model providers](../../stack/llm-providers/) when
you want to change, or when a rate limit forces the issue.

</Aside>

<Aside type="note" title="If your project only offers `anon` and `service_role`">


Supabase renamed and reworked its keys: `anon` became the **publishable** key
(`sb_publishable_…`) and `service_role` became the **secret** key
(`sb_secret_…`). Projects created before the change may still show only the
old pair, under the **Legacy API Keys** tab.

Those keep working until Supabase retires them at the end of 2026. Paste the
`service_role` key into `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` and carry on — everything in
this workshop behaves the same.

</Aside>

<Aside type="danger" title="The secret key bypasses every database security rule">


It belongs on your server and nowhere else. Never in frontend code, a
screenshot, a commit, or a chat message.

`.env` is already in `.gitignore` — check that it stays there. Once a key is
pushed to GitHub it is in the history forever and must be rotated.

</Aside>

## Prove it works

Run the tests. They need **no API key and no network**:

```bash
uv run --extra dev pytest
```

```text
.................                                   [100%]
17 passed
```

Then start the server:

```bash
uv run fastapi dev main.py
```

## Expected result

Open [http://localhost:8000/health](http://localhost:8000/health). You want:

```json
{"ok": true, "database": true, "provider": "google",
 "model": "gemini-flash-latest", "web_search": false}
```

Also open [http://localhost:8000/docs](http://localhost:8000/docs) — FastAPI generates that from your code,
and you'll use it to test the deployed version later. It follows your system's
light/dark setting: Swagger UI has had a dark theme since 5.31, and `app/main.py`
adds the few lines that switch it on.

## Install the client

The frontend is a separate Vite + React app in `client/`, with its own
dependencies. It needs **Node.js 20+** (`node --version`). From the repo root, in
a second terminal:

```bash
cd client
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open [http://localhost:5173](http://localhost:5173). You'll get the demo UI with
**Backend URL** already pointing at `http://localhost:8000` — leave it there for
now. You won't have anything to ask it until step 7; this is just to confirm both
halves install.

<Aside type="note" title="Two terminals from here on">

The backend runs from `app/`, the frontend from `client/`. Neither reloads the
other, so keep both running while you build.

</Aside>

## What usually goes wrong

<details>
<summary><code>database: false</code></summary>


Your `SUPABASE_URL` or key is wrong, or the project is paused. Free projects
pause after about a week idle — open the Supabase dashboard and resume it.

You haven't created the tables yet either — that's [step 2](../02-database/).
`database: false` at this point is expected if you've skipped ahead.

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>RuntimeError: Missing environment variable: LLM_API_KEY</code></summary>


Working as intended — config fails loudly at startup rather than mysteriously
at request time. Check `.env` exists in `app/` and that there are no quotes
around the values.

If you're following an older copy of this workshop, the variable used to be
called `GEMINI_API_KEY`. That name still works.

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>uv: command not found</code> after installing</summary>


The installer added it to a shell profile that your current terminal hasn't
read. Open a new terminal, or `source ~/.bashrc` / `source ~/.zshrc`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Python version errors</summary>


You don't need to fix your system Python. `uv python install 3.12` then
`uv sync` again — uv will use its own.

</details>

## What's next

You have an environment. Now it needs somewhere to put things.
